CheckTitle: KMS enclave key attestation binds at least two distinct PCR values
CheckType: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Description: **Enclave-scoped KMS keys** are evaluated on the breadth of their attestation conditions: every sensitive `Allow` statement must reference at least two distinct `kms:RecipientAttestation:*` bindings. `ImageSha384` collapses with `PCR0`; custom PCR IDs beyond 0-4 and 8 count toward the threshold.
Risk: `PCR0` alone (the enclave image hash) can be satisfied by any enclave built from the same EIF, allowing image-drift and supply-chain substitutions to preserve KMS access. A single-binding condition weakens the **integrity** the attestation was supposed to provide.

Code.NativeIaC:
```yaml
Condition:
  StringEqualsIgnoreCase:
    kms:RecipientAttestation:PCR0: <expected-pcr0>
    kms:RecipientAttestation:PCR1: <expected-pcr1>  # critical: second distinct PCR binding
```
Code.Other:
1. Include at least two distinct `kms:RecipientAttestation:PCR<N>` condition keys per sensitive Allow statement.
2. Prefer combinations such as `PCR0 + PCR1` (image + kernel), `PCR0 + PCR8` (image + signing certificate), or `PCR0 + custom PCR`.
3. Reject policies whose only binding is `PCR0` or `ImageSha384` because they collapse to a single measurement.
Code.Terraform:
```hcl
condition {
  test = "StringEqualsIgnoreCase"
  variable = "kms:RecipientAttestation:PCR1"  # critical: second distinct PCR binding
  values = [var.expected_pcr1]
}
```

Recommendation.Text: Apply **defense in depth** to the attestation contract: require multiple distinct PCR measurements so image-only substitutions and partial supply-chain compromises cannot preserve KMS access on their own.
